column1: unstinting§Unstinting praise for a first draft is a disservice.§对初稿**毫无保留**的赞美其实是帮倒忙。
unsubstantiated§An unsubstantiated figure repeated often enough becomes a fact.§一个**未经证实的**数字重复得够多就成了事实。
unsuitable§The room is unsuitable for lectures and perfect for rehearsal.§这个房间**不适合**讲课，排练却正合适。
unsure§Being unsure in print is more useful than false confidence.§在文字里承认**不确定**，比虚假的自信更有用。
unswerving§An unswerving line of poplars marks the old boundary.§一排**笔直不偏**的白杨标出了旧界线。
unvaried§An unvaried tone makes even good news sound like a warning.§**一成不变**的语调让好消息听起来也像警告。
unverified§Mark every unverified date with a question mark.§给每个**未经核实**的日期都加上问号。
unwieldy§An unwieldy title kept a good paper from being cited.§**笨重**的标题让一篇好论文无人引用。
unwitting§An unwitting accomplice is still named in the report.§**无意中**的共犯仍会被写进报告。
unyielding§Unyielding rock forced the road around the whole hill.§**坚硬**的岩石迫使道路绕过整座山。
uplift§The uplift of the whole range is about a millimetre a year.§整条山脉的**抬升**大约每年一毫米。
uprise§A low hill uprises where the two fields meet.§两块田交界处**隆起**一座矮丘。
urgency§Manufactured urgency is how bad decisions get made.§人为制造的**紧迫感**，正是坏决定产生的方式。
usurp§Convenience has usurped the place that judgement used to hold.§便利已经**篡夺**了判断力从前的位置。
usurper§The usurper's coins are commoner than the rightful king's.§**篡位者**的钱币比正统国王的更常见。
utilitarian§A utilitarian argument settles nothing when the values differ.§价值观不同时，**功利主义的**论证解决不了任何问题。
vacillate§The needle vacillated between two readings for an hour.§指针在两个读数之间**摇摆**了一小时。
vacillation§Vacillation is a decision to let someone else decide.§**犹豫不决**是一种让别人替你决定的决定。
vacuous§A vacuous truth is true because nothing satisfies the condition.§**空洞**的真命题之所以为真，是因为没有东西满足前提。
vagary§The vagaries of the postal service delayed the reply by a month.§邮政系统的**反复无常**让回复迟了一个月。
vagueness§Vagueness in a contract is expensive exactly once.§合同里的**含糊**只会昂贵地代价一次。
validate§Validate the input before you trust the output.§在相信输出之前先**校验**输入。
validity§Internal validity and external validity pull in opposite directions.§内部**效度**与外部效度朝相反方向拉扯。
valor§Valor in the citation often means someone else's plan failed.§嘉奖令里的“**英勇**”，往往意味着别人的计划失败了。
vanquish§Doubt is not vanquished; it is put to work.§怀疑不是被**战胜**的，而是被派上用场的。
vapid§A vapid title kills a book faster than a hostile review.§**平淡**的书名比恶评更快地害死一本书。
variegate§Variegated leaves grow more slowly than plain ones.§**花叶**品种比绿叶品种长得慢。
vector§The vector has a direction as well as a magnitude.§**矢量**既有大小，也有方向。
veer§The conversation veered into a subject nobody had prepared for.§谈话**转向**了一个谁也没准备的话题。
venality§Venality at the customs house was priced and predictable.§海关的**贪腐**明码标价，也可以预料。
venerability§Venerability is not an argument, though it is often used as one.§**年高德劭**不是论据，尽管常被当作论据。
venerate§We venerate the first edition and read the fourth.§我们**敬奉**第一版，读的却是第四版。
veneration§Veneration of a text prevents anyone from editing it.§对文本的**崇敬**使谁也不敢编辑它。
vengeful§A vengeful memory is an expensive thing to keep.§**怀恨**的记忆是一件昂贵的东西。
verbalization§Verbalization of a skill can temporarily make you worse at it.§把一项技能**说清楚**，反而会让你暂时做得更差。
verbose§Verbose in the first draft, terse in the fourth.§初稿**冗长**，第四稿简练。
verdant§A verdant strip along the river marks the flood line.§河边一条**翠绿**的带子标出了洪水线。
verisimilitude§Verisimilitude is not truth and is often mistaken for it.§**逼真**不是真实，却常被误认为真实。
versatility§Versatility is undervalued until something breaks.§**多才多艺**在出事之前一直被低估。
vestige§A vestige of the old spelling survives in one surname.§旧拼法的**痕迹**留存在一个姓氏里。
vestigial§A vestigial staircase leads to a floor that was removed.§一段**残余**的楼梯通往一个已被拆除的楼层。
vet§They vetted every applicant and missed the obvious one.§他们**审查**了每一位申请者，却漏掉了最明显的那个。
vex§The question has vexed historians since the letters surfaced.§自这些信件出现以来，这个问题一直**困扰**着史学家。
viable§A viable seed can wait in the soil for eighty years.§**有生命力**的种子能在土里等上八十年。
vibrant§Vibrant is what a brochure says about a street with a problem.§宣传册用“**充满活力**”来形容一条有问题的街。
vicarious§Vicarious liability makes the employer answer for the employee.§**替代责任**让雇主为雇员负责。
vicious§A vicious circle is broken at whatever point is cheapest.§**恶性**循环要在代价最小的那一点打破。
vigilant§Vigilant is exhausting; systems exist so people need not be.§**警惕**很耗人，制度的存在就是为了让人不必如此。
vignette§A vignette of four lines told us more than the chapter.§四行的**小品**文告诉我们的比整章还多。
vile§Vile weather in June is remembered longer than fine weather in July.§六月的**恶劣**天气比七月的好天气被记得更久。
vilify§To vilify a predecessor is the cheapest way to look new.§**诋毁**前任是显得自己新颖的最廉价方式。
villainous§A villainous handwriting is not evidence of a villain.§难看的字迹并不能证明写字的人是**恶棍**。
vindicate§Time vindicated a method that had been laughed at.§时间为一种曾被嘲笑的方法**正了名**。
vindication§Vindication is quieter than accusation and travels less far.§**昭雪**比指控安静，传播的范围也更小。
vindictive§A vindictive clause was inserted and later removed.§一条**报复性**的条款被塞了进去，后来又删掉了。
violently§The two accounts differ violently on one detail.§这两份记述在一个细节上**分歧极大**。
virtuosity§Virtuosity without a reason is a kind of noise.§没有理由的**炫技**是一种噪音。
viscous§Traffic was viscous rather than stationary.§车流是**黏滞**的，而不是完全静止。
visionary§A visionary is a planner whose timing was wrong.§**空想家**是一个时机不对的规划者。
vitiate§A single leading question can vitiate an entire interview.§一个诱导性问题就能使整场访谈**失效**。
vitriolic§Vitriolic criticism is remembered; useful criticism is used.§**刻薄的**批评被记住，有用的批评被采纳。
vivacious§Vivacious in company, she wrote in complete silence.§她在人群中**活泼**，写作时却完全安静。
vocal§Vocal music was banned here for sixty years.§**声乐**在这里被禁了六十年。
vocalize§Cats vocalize at humans and rarely at each other.§猫对人**发声**，很少对彼此发声。
voluble§Voluble on paper and silent in person is a common combination.§**落笔滔滔**、当面沉默，是常见的组合。
voluminous§Voluminous skirts made the doorways a daily problem.§**蓬大**的裙子让门口成了每天的难题。
voracious§A voracious appetite for detail can crowd out the argument.§对细节的**贪求**可能挤掉论证本身。
